# Review: `compositions/webapp-aws.yaml` + `claims/*` — 🔴 Request changes

Two blocking findings. The individual changes are each recoverable-ish; **together** they remove the last recovery path for prod data, so I won't approve this as a single PR regardless of how the deletion-policy question lands.

| # | Finding | Severity | AC violated |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `deletionPolicy: Delete` applied to stateful MRs (RDS, S3, KMS) across both envs | 🔴 Blocking | 2, 7 |
| 2 | Bucket versioning removed | 🔴 Blocking | 1 |
| 3 | Combined: `Delete` + no versioning (+ `forceDestroy`?) = unrecoverable | 🔴 Blocking | 1, 2 |
| 4 | Single composition mutating prod and dev in one revision | 🟠 Major | 7 |
| 5 | CRR / connection-secret fallout | 🟠 Major | 3 |

---

## What I read the diff as doing

I don't have the literal patch hunks, so correct me if this is off — but "provider-wide" is the phrase that worries me most, because **`deletionPolicy` is not a provider-level field.** There is no knob on `ProviderConfig` or `DeploymentRuntimeConfig` for it. It exists only on individual managed resources (`spec.deletionPolicy`), so a "provider-wide" change has to be one of:

```yaml
# (a) a YAML anchor merged into every base
x-defaults: &mr-defaults
  deletionPolicy: Delete            # <-- added
  providerConfigRef:
    name: aws-dev

resources:
  - name: assets-bucket
    base:
      apiVersion: s3.aws.upbound.io/v1beta1
      kind: Bucket
      spec:
        <<: *mr-defaults
```

…or (b) it was pasted into each `base.spec` by hand, or (c) a kustomize patch over the rendered composition. **All three mean the same thing at runtime: every composed resource, in every environment, is now deletable by Crossplane.** Please say which it is in the PR description, because (c) also silently applies to any *other* composition in the same kustomization.

Two notes on the field itself:

- `deletionPolicy` is **deprecated** since Crossplane v1.11 in favour of `managementPolicies`. New code should use `managementPolicies`; when `managementPolicies` is set to anything other than the default `["*"]`, it takes precedence over `deletionPolicy`. If some MRs in this repo already set `managementPolicies`, this new `deletionPolicy: Delete` is a **no-op on those and effective on the rest** — an inconsistency that is very hard to reason about during an incident. Pick one field.
- `Delete` is already the default. So if the motivation was "make dev teardown actually clean up AWS resources so we stop paying for orphans," the change is a no-op for that goal unless something was previously `Orphan`. Which suggests the real intent was to *remove* existing `Orphan` settings. Please confirm.

---

## Finding 1 — 🔴 `deletionPolicy: Delete` on stateful resources

`deletionPolicy` controls what happens to the **external AWS resource** when the MR object is deleted. The thing people underestimate is how many ordinary operations delete the MR object:

- `kubectl delete xwebapp` / claim delete
- deleting the claim's **namespace**
- **Argo CD / Flux prune** — including on a *rename*: change `resources[].name` from `assets-bucket` to `app-assets` and you get a new MR plus a pruned old one
- removing an entry from the composition (see Finding 2 — this is exactly what the versioning change does)
- an XR losing its claim binding

With `compositionUpdatePolicy: Automatic` (the default), a merged composition revision reaches **existing prod XRs on the next reconcile**, unprompted.

Blast radius per composed resource:

| Composed resource | On MR delete with `Delete` | Recoverable? |
|---|---|---|
| `rds.aws.upbound.io/Instance` | `DeleteDBInstance` | Only from snapshot; **not at all** if `skipFinalSnapshot: true` |
| `s3/Bucket` | `DeleteBucket` (fails unless `forceDestroy: true`) | Only from versions — which Finding 2 removes |
| `kms/Key` | schedules key deletion (`deletionWindowInDays`) | ⚠️ After the window, **anything encrypted with it is gone even if the bucket/DB were orphaned** |
| `eks/Cluster`, `NodeGroup` | deleted | Yes, recreatable (outage only) |
| `iam/Role`, `Policy`, `User` | deleted | Yes |
| `acm/Certificate`, `cloudfront/Distribution` | deleted | Yes (CloudFront disable+delete is slow) |

Two safety nets partially save you and both are traps:

1. **`deletionProtection: true` on the RDS instance** (required by AC 2) makes the delete API call fail. The MR then sits in `Deleting` with its finalizer forever, `Synced=False`. That's *good* — but the on-call fix people reach for is "set `deletionProtection: false` to unstick it," which converts the safety net into the loss event. Make sure the runbook says "restore `Orphan` / drop `Delete` from `managementPolicies`, not deletion protection."
2. **`forceDestroy` on the bucket** — please confirm its current value in the composition. `forceDestroy: true` + `deletionPolicy: Delete` + versioning suspended = every object *and* every historical version deleted in one reconcile.

**Fix:** scope deletability by environment, and default stateful resources closed. Don't ship a global `Delete`.

---

## Finding 2 — 🔴 Bucket versioning dropped

Direct violation of **AC 1** (versioning enabled). Three consequences beyond the checkbox:

**a) It breaks prod cross-region replication, hard.** S3 CRR requires versioning `Enabled` on *both* source and destination. `BucketReplicationConfiguration` will fail with `InvalidRequest: Versioning must be 'Enabled' on the bucket to apply a replication configuration`, that MR goes `Synced=False`, and the XR never reaches `Ready=True`. If replication was already live, existing replicated objects stay but **new writes stop replicating** — a silent DR/RPO breach that no readiness gate catches unless you're alerting on `BucketReplicationConfiguration` conditions specifically.

**b) You cannot "remove" versioning — only suspend it.** With the Upjet provider, versioning is its own MR (`s3.aws.upbound.io/v1beta1, kind: BucketVersioning`). Deleting that entry from the composition deletes the MR, and — **because of Finding 1** — the provider then destroys the external resource, which sets the bucket to `Suspended`. Post-suspension:

- existing versions remain (and keep billing) but are no longer created for new writes
- overwrites and deletes become **permanent**, `null` version ID
- lifecycle rules keyed on `NoncurrentVersion*` go inert — you may silently stop expiring old versions, or stop transitioning them
- MFA delete and Object Lock stop functioning; if any bucket has Object Lock enabled, S3 **rejects** the suspension and the MR wedges

Note the ordering hazard: if this had been `deletionPolicy: Orphan`, dropping the `BucketVersioning` entry would have left versioning enabled and merely unmanaged. The two halves of this PR interact.

**c) Why was it dropped?** If the motivation was a flapping/late-init fight between `Bucket` and `BucketVersioning` (a known annoyance on older provider versions where both could touch versioning), the fix is `managementPolicies` on the noisy field or pinning the provider version — not deleting the resource. Please state the motivation in the PR.

---

## Finding 3 — 🔴 The combination

Ordered as written, a single `kubectl delete claim` (or an Argo prune of a renamed resource) on prod now yields: bucket suspended → no versions for new objects → bucket deleted (with `forceDestroy`, contents and all) → RDS deleted → KMS key scheduled for deletion, so even an orphaned artefact would be unreadable. **There is no step in that chain with a recovery path.** Please split this into two PRs so the deletion-policy change can be reviewed against a bucket that still has versioning.

---

## Finding 4 — 🟠 Environment isolation (AC 7)

AC 7 says changing prod must not modify dev and vice versa. A single `Composition` shared by both claims with an env-agnostic `deletionPolicy` fails that: the dev-motivated change lands on prod automatically. Idiomatic Crossplane options, roughly in order of preference:

1. Patch the policy from `spec.parameters.environment` (below) — one composition, env-derived behaviour.
2. Two compositions selected by `compositionSelector.matchLabels.environment`, so dev and prod resolve to different revisions.
3. Pin prod: `compositionUpdatePolicy: Manual` + explicit `compositionRevisionRef` on the prod claim, so revisions are promoted deliberately.

I'd like (1) or (2) **plus** (3) for prod.

---

## Finding 5 — 🟠 Secret + CRR fallout (AC 3)

- Deleting an MR deletes its connection secret. If you orphan the RDS instance but let the secret go, you've orphaned a database **nobody has the master password for**. Please confirm the DB credentials are published to an external store (`publishConnectionDetailsTo.configRef` → a `StoreConfig` backed by AWS Secrets Manager) and not only `writeConnectionSecretToRef` in-cluster.
- Confirm the **destination** bucket in `us-west-2` still has its own `BucketVersioning` — the diff may have removed one and not the other, which fails CRR just as effectively.
- Confirm `BucketPublicAccessBlock` and `BucketServerSideEncryptionConfiguration` entries are untouched (AC 1). If the same hunk removed them, that's a third blocker.

---

## Suggested patch

**Restore versioning on both buckets:**

```yaml
- name: assets-bucket-versioning
  base:
    apiVersion: s3.aws.upbound.io/v1beta1
    kind: BucketVersioning
    spec:
      forProvider:
        bucketSelector:
          matchControllerRef: true
        versioningConfiguration:
          - status: Enabled
  patches:
    - type: FromCompositeFieldPath
      fromFieldPath: spec.parameters.region
      toFieldPath: spec.forProvider.region

- name: replica-bucket-versioning        # prod only, us-west-2
  base:
    apiVersion: s3.aws.upbound.io/v1beta1
    kind: BucketVersioning
    spec:
      forProvider:
        region: us-west-2
        bucketSelector:
          matchControllerRef: true
          matchLabels:
            role: replica
        versioningConfiguration:
          - status: Enabled
```

(`versioningConfiguration` is a **list** in the Upjet provider — easy thing to get wrong on the way back in.)

**Make deletability an environment-derived property, not a global default:**

```yaml
# stateful: assets-bucket, replica-bucket, rds-instance, kms-key
patches:
  - type: FromCompositeFieldPath
    fromFieldPath: spec.parameters.environment
    toFieldPath: spec.managementPolicies
    transforms:
      - type: map
        map:
          dev:  ["*"]
          prod: ["Observe", "Create", "Update", "LateInitialize"]   # no Delete => orphan
```

Non-string map values need Crossplane ≥ v1.12 / a recent `function-patch-and-transform`; if you're on something older, use option (2) from Finding 4 instead. Drop `deletionPolicy` entirely rather than leaving both fields set — the precedence rules are a footgun during an incident.

Stateless MRs (IAM, node groups, SGs, listeners, distribution) can keep `["*"]` in both envs; that's the part of the original intent worth keeping.

**Belt and braces for prod stateful resources** — a `Usage` guard makes the API server reject deletion outright, independent of policy fields:

```yaml
apiVersion: apiextensions.crossplane.io/v1beta1
kind: Usage
metadata:
  name: protect-prod-db
spec:
  reason: "Production database — delete requires explicit removal of this Usage"
  of:
    apiVersion: rds.aws.upbound.io/v1beta1
    kind: Instance
    resourceRef:
      name: webapp-prod-db
```

---

## Guardrails so this can't recur

Policy at the **rendered MR** level, not the Composition level — a composition can set these fields via patches, so linting the composition YAML alone misses it:

```yaml
apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1
kind: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy
metadata:
  name: prod-stateful-mrs-not-deletable
spec:
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
      - apiGroups: ["s3.aws.upbound.io", "rds.aws.upbound.io", "kms.aws.upbound.io"]
        apiVersions: ["*"]
        resources:  ["*"]
        operations: ["CREATE", "UPDATE"]
  validations:
    - expression: |
        object.metadata.?labels["environment"].orValue("") != "prod" ||
        ( has(object.spec.managementPolicies) &&
          !("*" in object.spec.managementPolicies) &&
          !("Delete" in object.spec.managementPolicies) )
      message: "prod stateful managed resources must not be Crossplane-deletable"
```

And in CI, gate on rendered output:

```bash
crossplane render examples/xwebapp-prod.yaml compositions/webapp-aws.yaml functions.yaml \
  | kyverno apply policies/ --resource -            # or conftest test -
```

That catches both halves of this PR: the missing `BucketVersioning` and the `Delete` policy on prod.

---

## Merge checklist

- [ ] Split into two PRs; versioning restoration lands first
- [ ] State which mechanism applied `deletionPolicy` "provider-wide" and whether it leaks into other compositions
- [ ] State the motivation for dropping versioning (flapping MR? cost? CRR error?)
- [ ] Report current `forceDestroy` and `skipFinalSnapshot` values
- [ ] `crossplane render` diff for **both** dev and prod XRs attached to the PR; only intended fields change
- [ ] Dev soak: apply, then `aws s3api get-bucket-versioning` → `Enabled`; `crossplane beta trace xwebapp/<name>` all `Ready=True`
- [ ] Prod dry run: confirm `BucketReplicationConfiguration` reconciles `Synced=True`
- [ ] Prod claim set to `compositionUpdatePolicy: Manual` with a pinned `compositionRevisionRef`
- [ ] DB credentials confirmed in an external `StoreConfig`, not only an in-cluster Secret
- [ ] Rollback note in the PR: **suspended versioning cannot be un-suspended retroactively** — objects overwritten during the window are unrecoverable

Happy to re-review as soon as the two changes are separated; the dev-teardown-cost problem behind #1 is real and the env-scoped `managementPolicies` patch should solve it cleanly.
